title: Your Overdraft Is a Safety Cushion? £500 for a Year Costs About £100 😱💳 #shorts
description:
Owe £500 on your overdraft for a year and, at the average rate, it costs about £100 in interest: about the same as a credit card.

The numbers (Bank of England, Money and Credit, September 2026, published 29 October): the average effective interest rate on interest-charging overdrafts is 20.79%, and on interest-charging credit cards 21.71%: both just over a fifth a year. So £500 overdrawn for a year costs about £103.95 at the overdraft average (about £100), and £108.55 at the credit card average. For comparison, the average rate on new personal loans is 9.85%.

The strange part: going past your limit (an unarranged overdraft) used to cost far more, often through daily fees. Since April 2020 the FCA's rules mean banks can't charge more for an unarranged overdraft than an arranged one, and can't charge fixed fees for overdraft borrowing: just one interest rate.

Sources: https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/statistics/money-and-credit/2026/september-2026 · https://www.fca.org.uk/news/press-releases/millions-customers-together-save-nearly-1billion-due-overdraft-rule-changes · https://www.fca.org.uk/data/changes-overdraft-charges

Averages include all interest-charging accounts; your own bank's advertised rate (EAR) may be higher or lower, so check yours. Rates as at 31 October 2026. General education, not financial advice.
